interface.title: LLM literature screener (v0.1.0, Streamlit app)
interface.field: Evidence synthesis / systematic reviews (health and clinical research)
interface.stage_of_work: Title-and-abstract screening, after the database search and before full-text review
interface.what_it_is_for: Rank bibliographic records against a review protocol (PICO criteria), set an exclusion threshold on decisions the team has already made so a target recall of known inclusions is kept, and export the ranked records, a self-contained HTML report, and PRISMA 2020 counts with a methods paragraph.

data.note: First I used the bundled synthetic example (26 invented records on exercise for chronic low back pain, with its protocol and 15 labelled records, 7 of them inclusions). Then I uploaded the test files records.ris and labels.csv. The uploaded protocol.yaml was never used: the app only reads the 'Or paste it here' box. That box starts with a placeholder template, so the template was used instead of the file (screens/035.webp, report title '<the review question>'). After I emptied the box, the run failed with 'The protocol must be a YAML mapping' even with protocol.yaml uploaded and re-uploaded (screens/036.webp, 039.webp, 040.webp). I worked around this by pasting the protocol text, and that run matched the bundled example exactly (screens/041.webp). All scoring used the mock keyword-overlap backend.

tree.general: Cut down how many records people must read in a systematic review while keeping almost every relevant study, and document the cut-down for reporting
tree.specific: Pre-screen titles and abstracts by scoring them against the protocol with a language model (hf for a local model, openai for an OpenAI-compatible server), calibrate an exclusion threshold for a target recall of the team's known inclusions, and export the report, PRISMA counts and ranked results; this run used only the mock keyword-overlap backend

features.name: Recall-target threshold calibration with Wilson CI
features.general: Pick a cut-off on a ranking score so that a chosen share of known positive items stays above it, then report the achieved recall with a confidence interval and a warning when there are few positives
features.specific: Set the 'Target recall on known inclusions' slider (0.80 to 1.00), upload labels, run screening, and read the exclusion threshold score, P(include), 'Known inclusions kept' and the 95% Wilson CI; fewer than 10 known inclusions triggers a warning
steps: Set the target recall on the slider
Read the threshold, kept inclusions, Wilson CI and any few-inclusions warning
Change the target and rerun to compare
serves_tasks: Set the exclusion cut-off so a target share of known relevant items is kept, and see the confidence interval
Read the warnings about how far the results can be trusted

features.name: Manual two-threshold override
features.general: Replace the automatic cut-off with hand-entered lower (exclude) and upper (include) score bounds, with the change recorded in the output
features.specific: Tick 'Set the threshold myself', type Exclusion threshold and Include threshold scores, rerun; the Calibration table reads 'Set by the user' and the methods paragraph says the team set the threshold
steps: Check the Decisions split and the Calibration rule in the report
serves_tasks: Set the cut-offs by hand instead of calibrating

features.name: Three-way decision split bar with score bands
features.general: Show how items fall into keep / borderline / drop as a stacked percentage bar and a table giving the score range that defines each band
features.specific: The Decisions card in the report: a segmented bar (Include / Uncertain / Exclude) with a table of counts, shares and score ranges, updated after each run
steps: Read the stacked bar and legend
Read the counts and score bands in the table
serves_tasks: See how items split into keep, borderline and drop

features.name: Interactive recall (work-saved) curve with threshold marker
features.general: Plot the share of known positives found against the share of items read in ranked order, next to a random-order baseline and a target line; hover for exact values, or switch to a table
features.specific: The 'Recall on the known inclusions' chart: a blue curve in the model's order, a grey random-order diagonal, a dashed 95% target line and a Threshold dot; hover shows a crosshair tooltip ('5 of 7 known inclusions after reading 6 records'); 'Show the curve as a table' lists 10% steps plus the threshold row. Some recall percentages do not match their counts: '70.3% found' and 78.6% for 5 of 7 (71.4%), 35.7% for 2 of 7 (28.6%)
steps: Hover along the curve to read the tooltip
Expand Show the curve as a table
serves_tasks: Check how early the known relevant items turn up in the ranking

features.name: Borderline-items review table with one-line reasons
features.general: List only the items just above the drop cut-off, ranked by score, each with a short machine-written reason, so people can look at the doubtful cases first
features.specific: The 'Uncertain records (N)' table: rank, title with year, journal and id, score, P(include) and reason ('Mentions 13 protocol terms (...)'); the 'Write one-line reasons' checkbox switches the reasons on or off
steps: Read the reasons; untick the option and rerun to compare (reasons become 'none')
serves_tasks: Read the reasons given for borderline items
Switch the short machine-written reasons on or off

features.name: PRISMA 2020 counts and auto-written methods paragraph
features.general: Turn a run's numbers into reporting-guideline flow counts and a ready-to-paste methods paragraph that describes deduplication, scoring, threshold rule and recall with its CI
features.specific: The PRISMA 2020 table (records identified, per source, duplicates removed, marked ineligible by automation tools, screened by the team, excluded by the team 'to be completed') and the Methods paragraph, also exported as prisma.md

serves_tasks: Inspect the reporting-guideline flow counts and a ready-to-use methods text

features.name: Results export in the input citation format, as a table and as a bundle

features.specific: 'Records with decisions (.ris)' gives records_screened.ris with lls_score, lls_p_include, lls_decision and lls_reason notes; 'Ranked results (CSV)' gives screening_results.csv (rank, id, title, label, score, p_include, decision, reason); 'Download all results (zip)' gives screening_results.zip
